2027-06-03.title: Third Thursday of the Apostles
2027-06-03.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: You are God's field, God's building
The seed is the word of God
2027-06-03.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), from Pentecost to the beginning of the Season of Summer (Kaitha): the Church remembers the apostles who, filled with the Holy Spirit, preached Christ and founded the Churches, among them the Church of India founded by Mar Thoma. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed at the three hours of the day. In the Latin calendar today is the memorial of St Charles Lwanga and his companions, the Martyrs of Uganda.
2027-06-03.verse: But as for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.
theo: In the first days of June the southwest monsoon reaches Kerala, and across the paddy fields of Palakkad and Kuttanad, in the hill farms of Idukki and Wayanad, farmers prepare the ground and sow. Today's Gospel could have been told in a Kerala village. “A sower went out to sow his seed; and as he sowed, some fell on the path and was trampled on, and the birds of the air ate it up. Some fell on the rock; and as it grew up, it withered for lack of moisture. Some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew with it and choked it. Some fell into good soil, and when it grew, it produced a hundredfold.” The first surprise is the sower himself. He throws seed generously, even where it seems wasted: on the beaten path, on the thin soil over rock, among the thorns. God does not ration his word to those who seem likely to receive it. Every person, even the hardest, hears the word at least once. Then Jesus cries out, “Let anyone with ears to hear listen!” The parable is not only a description; it is an appeal.

Jesus himself explains it: “Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.” The path is the heart where “the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved”: we hear on Sunday and have forgotten by the time we reach the church gate. The rock is the heart that receives the word with joy but has no root: a retreat, a feast, a moment of fervour, and then in the time of testing the faith falls away. The thorns are the heart that hears, but “as they go on their way, they are choked by the cares and riches and pleasures of life, and their fruit does not mature.” Notice the three thorns: cares, riches and pleasures. Worry and wealth and comfort are not obviously sins, but they can quietly choke the word. And the good soil: “these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.” Hold it fast, and wait. A farmer does not dig up his seed every morning to see if it has sprouted. He keeps the field, clears the weeds and trusts the rain. Fruit in the spiritual life takes the same patience.

Paul's letter shows what happens when a community is still poor soil. “I fed you with milk, not solid food, for you were not ready for solid food. Even now you are still not ready, for you are still of the flesh. For as long as there is jealousy and quarreling among you, are you not of the flesh?” The sign of spiritual infancy in Corinth was not a lack of gifts; it was faction. “For when one says, ‘I belong to Paul,’ and another, ‘I belong to Apollos,’ are you not merely human?” Paul refuses to be the head of a party: “What then is Apollos? What is Paul? Servants through whom you came to believe, as the Lord assigned to each. I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.” Parishes and dioceses can still divide around personalities, preferences and old grievances, and every such quarrel keeps a community on milk. The cure Paul offers is to look away from the servants to the Lord of the harvest: “For we are God’s servants, working together; you are God’s field, God’s building.” The Church is not the property of any preacher or group. She is God's field, sown by the apostles, watered by their successors, and made to grow by God alone.

The Latin Church today remembers the Martyrs of Uganda, St Charles Lwanga and his companions. Missionaries had arrived in Buganda only in 1879. Within a few years young men at the court of King Mwanga II, many of them royal pages, had received the word with joy and held it fast. When the king demanded what their faith forbade, they refused. On 3 June 1886, at Namugongo, Charles Lwanga and a group of companions were burned to death; others were killed in the months before and after, the youngest, Kizito, still a boy of about fourteen. Anglican Christians died with them. Pope Paul VI canonised the twenty-two Catholic martyrs in 1964 and in 1969 became the first Pope to visit Africa, going to Namugongo. Today Uganda's Church is one of the most vigorous in the world. The seed that fell on that good soil bore fruit a hundredfold, exactly as the parable says, with patient endurance.
outline: The monsoon arrives and the farmers sow: the parable told in a Kerala field.
God sows his word everywhere; let anyone with ears listen.
The devil, the time of testing, and the cares, riches and pleasures of life.
Factions keep a community on milk; we are God's field, God's building.
The Martyrs of Uganda, seed that bore fruit a hundredfold.
“Hold it fast in an honest and good heart.”
live: After Sunday's Qurbana this week, write down one sentence from the Gospel and read it every morning until the next Sunday.
Name the worry, the possession or the pleasure that most chokes your prayer, and give it to God in confession or in a concrete sacrifice.
Do not join any talk that divides your parish into parties; speak instead of what unites.
fathers: The good soil brings forth fruit through patience, because nothing we do is good unless we bear patiently the wrongs of our neighbours. The higher a person climbs, the more he finds in this world to endure; the fruit is not lost if it is guarded by patience.
The more often you mow us down, the more numerous we grow: the blood of Christians is seed.
magis: The word of the Lord is compared to a seed sown in a field; those who hear it with faith and are numbered among the little flock of Christ have truly received the kingdom.
Christ always gives his Church the gift of unity, but the Church must always pray and work to maintain, reinforce and perfect it.
Martyrdom is the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith: a witness even unto death, bearing witness to Christ who died and rose.
saints: Latin calendar: St Charles Lwanga and his twenty-one companions, Martyrs of Uganda, killed under King Mwanga II between 1885 and 1887 (Charles Lwanga at Namugongo on 3 June 1886); canonised by Pope Paul VI in 1964.

1–6 June: the third and fourth weeks of the Season of the Apostles. Tue 1: St Justin, martyr. Thu 3: in the Latin calendar, St Charles Lwanga and his companions, the Martyrs of Uganda. Fri 4: the Feast of the Sacred Heart of Jesus (Third Friday of the Apostles), and First Friday. Sat 5: the Feast of the Immaculate Heart of Mary (Third Saturday of the Apostles); in the Latin calendar also St Boniface. Sun 6: Fourth Sunday of the Apostles. June is the month of the Sacred Heart in popular devotion; in Kerala it is also the month the schools reopen and the monsoon rains arrive.
2027-06-03.prayer: Lord God, Lord of the harvest, you sow your word in every heart, on the path, on the rock and among the thorns. Break up the hard ground in us, give our faith deep roots, and clear away the cares, riches and pleasures that choke your word. Keep us from jealousy and factions, for we are your field and your building, and you alone give the growth. By the prayers of the Martyrs of Uganda, give us honest and good hearts that hold your word fast and bear fruit with patient endurance. Through Christ our Lord, to whom with you and the Holy Spirit be glory for ever. Amen.
altar: Every Holy Qurbana begins with the sowing of the word in the readings, and then the bread, fruit of the earth and of the patience of farmers, becomes the Body of the Lord. Let the word we hear and the Bread we receive find good soil in us.

2027-06-03.question: Which of the four soils is my heart today?

family.explain: When the monsoon comes, farmers sow seeds. Some seeds fall on the hard path and birds eat them. Some fall on rocks and dry up. Some fall among thorns and get choked. Some fall on good soil and grow into a big harvest. Jesus says that the seed is God's word. When we listen to the Bible and keep it in our hearts, it grows in us and makes us good and kind.
family.intention: We pray for farmers and for good rains this monsoon, and for those who suffer from floods.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one word of Jesus that our family will try to remember this week?”

illus: An old farmer in Wayanad, whose parents had come from Travancore in the years of the migration to Malabar, took his grandson to the field on the first morning of the monsoon. The boy watched him throw the seed and asked why he threw it so widely, even near the path where the birds were waiting. ‘Because I do not know which handful will grow,’ the old man said. ‘My father taught me: sow generously, keep the field clean, and leave the rest to God.’ Then he took off his towel, knelt at the edge of the field and made the sign of the cross over the wet earth. The grandson, who is now a priest, says that whenever he preaches he remembers that morning. ‘I throw the seed,’ he says. ‘I do not know which word will grow. God gives the growth.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, sower of the word, we open our hearts to you. Make them good soil, take away what hardens them, and let your word bear fruit in us. Amen.
share: The seed is the word of God (Luke 8:11). How do I receive the word on Sunday?
These have no root (Luke 8:13). When has my faith fallen away in a time of testing?
Choked by the cares and riches and pleasures of life (Luke 8:14). What chokes the word in me?
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth (1 Corinthians 3:6). Do I trust God with the fruit of my work?
pm.resp: Lord, make our hearts good soil.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that the word may be preached everywhere and received with honest hearts.
For parishes and dioceses wounded by divisions, that they may remember they are God's field and God's building.
For farmers in this season of sowing, for good rains, and for those affected by floods and landslides.
For the Church in Uganda and in all Africa, that the seed sown by the martyrs may keep bearing fruit.
For those whose faith has dried up in times of trial, that they may find roots again.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the sower and his word is the seed of eternal life. Give us honest and good hearts, keep us united as your field, and make us bear fruit with patient endurance. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the monsoon has come and the farmers are sowing. Jesus tells us about a sower who throws his seed everywhere, on the path, on the rock, among thorns and on good soil. God is that generous sower: he gives his word to everyone.

The seed is the word of God (Luke 8:11). Some hear it and the devil takes it away at once. Some receive it with joy, but have no root, and fall away when trouble comes. Some hear it, but the cares, riches and pleasures of life choke it. Which soil am I?

The good soil, Jesus says, is the heart that holds the word fast and bears fruit with patient endurance (Luke 8:15). Holding fast means remembering, praying over the word, living it. Patient endurance means not giving up when fruit is slow.

Saint Paul tells the Corinthians that their quarrels show they are still infants: one says, I belong to Paul, another, I belong to Apollos. Paul says: I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. You are God's field. Let us never divide our parish into parties; we all belong to Christ.

Today the Latin Church remembers the Martyrs of Uganda, young men who received the Gospel only a few years before they died for it. The seed fell on good soil, and today their Church is full of life. May God's word find such soil in us. Amen.
kids: Children, a farmer threw seeds. Some fell on the path, some on rocks, some among thorns, and some on good soil, where they grew into a big harvest.
Jesus says his word is the seed, and your heart is the soil. Listen to Jesus and keep his word in your heart, and it will grow into kindness and goodness!

As for what fell among the thorns, these are the ones who hear; but as they go on their way, they are choked by the cares and riches and pleasures of life, and their fruit does not mature.

concl: God sows generously; our hearts decide what becomes of the seed.
United as God's field, and patient like the martyrs, we will bear fruit a hundredfold.
2027-06-03.resolve: This week, keep the word, clear one thorn, and refuse every faction.
